title: Kalispell to Sandpoint, Lake Pend Oreille
summary: A forest highway from Glacier country into North Idaho, ending lakeside in Sandpoint.

segments.name: Segment 1 — Kootenai National Forest, West Glacier to Bonners Ferry
segments.blurb: Two-lane highway through Kootenai National Forest along the Kootenai River.

stops.name: Kootenai Falls
stops.note: Roadside stop on US-2, largest undammed falls in Montana.

stops.name: Troy, Montana
stops.note: Small riverside town near the Idaho line.

stops.name: Kootenai National Forest
stops.note: Forest corridor for most of the morning drive.

stops.name: Bonners Ferry
stops.note: Kootenai River crossing, gateway to the Idaho Panhandle.

expect.arrive: Two-lane US-2 through forest; Kootenai Falls is a short walk down from a large roadside pullout.
expect.parking: Kootenai Falls pullout is large and rarely full outside summer weekends.

paths.do: Stay on US-2, stop only for photos from the car.
Walk down to the falls viewpoint and swinging bridge.

segments.name: Segment 2 — US-95 south to Sandpoint, tamarack country
segments.blurb: Selkirk Mountains foothills, with a larch-viewing detour up Pack River.

stops.name: Kaniksu National Forest
stops.note: Forest boundary the highway runs through south of Bonners Ferry.

stops.name: Selkirk Mountains
stops.note: Range visible to the west for most of the drive.

stops.name: Upper Pack River Road
stops.note: Gravel side road off US-95 near Samuels; western larch turn gold in early October.

stops.name: Sandpoint Long Bridge
stops.note: Two-mile wooden-piling bridge crossing the lake into town.

expect.arrive: Highway drive with the Selkirks to the west; the Pack River detour is unpaved and only worth it if the larch are turning.

paths.do: Turn up gravel Upper Pack River Road for golden tamarack views.

segments.name: Segment 3 — Sandpoint lakeshore, afternoon into evening
segments.blurb: Lake Pend Oreille shoreline trails and the Schweitzer viewpoint above town.

stops.name: City Beach
stops.note: In-town lake beach and park, easy first stop.

stops.name: Pend d'Oreille Bay Trail
stops.note: 3.2-mile flat lakeside trail from Ponderay to Sandpoint.

stops.name: Sand Creek Trail
stops.note: Paved path along Sand Creek from downtown Sandpoint.

stops.name: Schweitzer Mountain Resort
stops.note: Viewpoint above town, weather and time permitting.

stops.name: Pend Oreille Scenic Byway
stops.note: SR-200 lakeshore drive east of town for evening light.

expect.arrive: City Beach is a short walk from downtown parking; the Long Bridge and open lake are right behind it.
expect.parking: Downtown Sandpoint street parking and the City Beach lot fill on nice afternoons.

paths.do: Walk the beach and watch boats on the lake.
Paved path along the creek from downtown, flat and short.
Continue along the lakeshore trail toward Ponderay.
